nodes.contract: A feasible finite-dimensional linear program with finite optimum has an equal dual optimum under the stated primal/dual formulation.

For a finite perfect graph and nonnegative weights, the maximum-weight stable-set value equals the fractional clique-cover optimum. This equality contract does not itself include an algorithmic complexity claim.
The complement of a perfect graph is perfect; under an explicit rational bit encoding and a promise/certificate of perfectness, weighted stable-set optimization is polynomial-time.

The quantum maximum of a weighted squared Pauli profile depends only on the frustration graph; hbar-perfect graphs are those for which it equals the weighted independent-set value for all nonnegative weights.
For a pure n-qubit state, the fourth Pauli moment defines the order-2 stabilizer Renyi entropy and vanishes exactly for pure stabilizer states.
The full n-qubit Pauli frustration graph is an isolated identity plus the binary symplectic graph; maximal abelian Pauli supports are maximum independent sets of size 2^n.
Relative to stabilizer operations as the free subtheory, states outside the stabilizer free set carry nonstabilizerness, also called magic.
STAB_n is the convex hull of all pure n-qubit stabilizer states.
Full RoM is the minimum l1 norm of a signed affine decomposition of rho over pure stabilizer states, with value one exactly on STAB_n.
A finite set M of nonidentity Hermitian n-qubit Pauli observables maps rho to b_M(rho)=(tr(P rho))_{P in M}.
STAB(M) is the image of STAB_n under the Pauli expectation window.

RoM_M(rho) is the minimum l1 norm of a signed affine decomposition of b_M(rho) over STAB(M); projection implies RoM_M(rho)<=RoM(rho), so RoM_M(rho)>1 is a sound magic certificate. With M held fixed, it is not a monotone under all stabilizer operations.
G_M has one vertex per measured Pauli and an edge exactly for anticommuting pairs; independent sets are pairwise commuting contexts.
STAB(M)=conv{v_(S,f)} over inclusion-maximal commuting contexts S and phase-aware admissible signs f.
The target and Varela source claim RoM_M(E(rho))<=RoM_M(rho) for every trace-preserving stabilizer operation E while M is held fixed.
nodes.counterexample: For one qubit M={X,Z} and rho with Bloch vector (1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2),0), RoM_M(rho)=1. The free Clifford Rx(pi/2) maps the visible coordinates to (1/sqrt(2),+/-1/sqrt(2)), so RoM_M(E(rho))=sqrt(2). Covariance under jointly rotating both state and window remains valid.

nodes.contract: Finite linear-program duality expresses exact reduced RoM as max b.y+mu subject to one absolute-value constraint for every admissible maximal-context vertex.
The exact V-representation can be exponentially large and general reduced-polytope membership is NP-hard; consequently no polynomial algorithm in n,m exists for arbitrary exact instances unless P=NP.

For commuting Hermitian Pauli representatives, the product phase defines a linear syndrome on ker(M_S); independent generator eigenvalues extend consistently, so B_S is a nonempty affine coset of size 2^rank(M_S).
Within a commuting context, phase-free kernel relations with their +/- identity syndromes are exactly the parity checks defining the admissible sign assignments.
The sign-relaxed polytope retains all +/- assignments on every maximal commuting context, including assignments not compatible with Pauli product relations.
relaxed_RoM_M is the minimum l1 signed affine decomposition of b_M(rho) over the sign-relaxed polytope.
For nonnegative vertex weights w, alpha_w(G) is the maximum total weight over all independent sets of G.
STAB(M) is contained in the sign-relaxed polytope and therefore relaxed_RoM_M(rho)<=RoM_M(rho).
An inclusion-minimal Pauli product relation is active exactly when its support is pairwise commuting and therefore imposes a joint-eigenvalue parity check.
M has no Pauli-active dependency iff every commuting context admits every deterministic sign assignment.
STAB(M) equals the sign-relaxed polytope iff M has no Pauli-active dependency; in that regime exact and relaxed reduced RoM coincide.

For every measured coordinate i, a maximal commuting context containing i and a one-sign flip yield a vertex difference proportional to e_i; hence the relaxed primal is feasible for every b in R^m and bounded below by one.
Strong LP duality turns relaxed RoM into a maximization over (y,mu) with one absolute-value constraint per relaxed vertex.
For fixed S,y,mu, maximizing over all sign assignments gives sum_{i in S}|y_i|+|mu|.
relaxed_RoM_M(rho)=max b.y+mu subject to alpha_|y|(G_M)+|mu|<=1; a maximum-weight independent set supplies a violated constraint when one exists.
Under no Pauli-active dependency, the MWIS-constrained relaxed dual is the exact reduced-RoM dual.
G is perfect iff every induced subgraph G' satisfies chromatic_number(G')=clique_number(G').
For every finite graph and nonnegative weight, weighted alpha <= weighted theta <= weighted fractional clique-cover number.

For a perfect graph, {z>=0:alpha_z<=1} is the convex hull of clique incidence vectors including the empty clique. The target derives this locally from weighted stable-set/fractional-cover duality and downward closure.
For a perfect graph and nonnegative weights, weighted alpha=weighted theta=weighted fractional clique-cover number.
If M has no Pauli-active dependency and G_M is perfect, RoM_M(rho)=max(1,max_Q sum_{P in Q}|tr(P rho)|).
For a pairwise anticommuting Pauli set Q and any state rho, sum_{P in Q}tr(P rho)^2<=1.
In the solvable regime, RoM_M(rho)<=sqrt(clique_number(G_M)) for every rho.
A state supported on the +1 eigenspace of |Q|^{-1/2}sum_{P in Q}P has equal expectations 1/sqrt(|Q|) on Q and attains sqrt(|Q|).
In the solvable regime, sup_rho RoM_M(rho)=sqrt(clique_number(G_M)).
The binary-symplectic Gram matrix of a pairwise anticommuting n-qubit Pauli family implies cardinality at most 2n+1.
The 2n Jordan-Wigner Majoranas plus global parity form K_(2n+1), have only an inactive full-support dependency, and therefore lie in the solvable regime.
Among solvable n-qubit measurement windows, max_M sup_rho RoM_M(rho)=sqrt(2n+1), with equality exactly when M contains a maximum anticommuting clique.

Promise evaluation only: given rational/finite-precision expectation values together with a certified no-active-dependency, perfect-graph measurement window, the maximum-weight clique in the closed form is polynomial-time computable. The paper does not establish a polynomial-time end-to-end recognizer for the no-active condition.
Assuming arbitrary Clifford diagonalization of each commuting family, a perfect frustration graph partitions M into clique_number(G_M) jointly measurable settings.
Local XYZ, open Ising path, Majorana tree and Jordan-Wigner families have the stated perfect frustration graphs, no Pauli-active dependencies and the stated witness capacities.
RoM_(C M Cdag)(rho)=RoM_M(Cdag rho C), retaining the signed conjugated observables as coordinates.
Clifford conjugation preserves commutation, anticommutation and Pauli product relations, hence preserves G_M, perfectness and the active/inactive status of dependencies.
Every Clifford image of a solvable seed window has the same graph, solvability condition, closed form and witness capacity.
For a specified state ensemble, rotation list and threshold, detection coverage is the fraction with max_l RoM_(C_l M C_ldag)(rho)>1.
At n=8, evaluate four seed windows on 10,000 Haar states across K Clifford rotations and on 400 hardware-efficient variational states at each listed depth.
At n=8, a common batch of 10,000 Haar-random pure states is evaluated for K in {1,5,10,20,50,100} Clifford rotations.
At n=8, a common batch of 400 states per depth L in {5,10,15,30,50} is generated by independent one-qubit RY/RZ rotations followed by a periodic CZ ring.

For the reported finite samples, adding Clifford rotations increases coverage, especially for the Jordan-Wigner and Majorana-tree windows; larger capacity is empirically associated with higher detection rates.
The supplied source bundle lacks code, raw data, random seeds, rotation sampler details, angle distributions and numerical tolerance; the empirical branch cannot be marked reproduced.

nodes.contract: x_P(rho)=tr(P rho)^2 defines a nonnegative profile; weighted directional concentration and its self-collision are distinct nonlinear summaries.
nodes.domain_override: This appendix branch uses the full qubit Pauli set including identity; it does not inherit the main branch's nonidentity-only window assumption.

nodes.contract: Squaring Pauli expectations removes eigenvalue signs; a pure stabilizer profile is the incidence vector of a commuting support, and every independent set extends into such a profile.
For nonnegative weights, max over STAB_n of sum w_P tr(P sigma)^2 equals alpha_w(G_M); sign dependencies do not affect this quadratic optimum.
A strict gap beta(G,w)>alpha_w(G) certifies nonstabilizerness; hbar-perfect graphs have no witness from this quadratic family.
For d=2^n, sum_P tr(P rho)^2=d tr(rho^2), defining a normalized Pauli distribution.
Maximum independent sets of the full Pauli graph are maximal abelian supports of size d; pure stabilizer Pauli distributions are uniform on them, and conversely.
For pure psi, M2(psi)=H2(Xi)-log alpha(G_full), and it vanishes exactly when Xi is uniform on a maximum independent set, equivalently psi is a stabilizer state.
For mixed rho, the normalized fourth-moment identity includes -S2(rho); it can be negative and therefore is not by itself a mixed-state magic measure.
The MWIS with weights tr(P rho)^2 equals d times the largest purity retained after dephasing rho in a stabilizer basis and is at most d tr(rho^2).
A graph-theoretic mixed-state magic bound connecting the moment identity to a stabilizer threshold has not been established.

For n>=2, the full Pauli frustration graph is imperfect with exponentially larger chromatic than clique number, and each maximal commuting context carries exponentially many independent sign constraints.
When the graph is perfect but active dependencies remain, MWIS is tractable while admissible-sign optimization becomes coset decoding; efficiently decodable dependency-code classes are open.
With no active dependencies but an imperfect graph, replacing MWIS by weighted Lovasz theta yields a sound polynomial-time lower bound; characterizing tight cases is open.
